[Review after completing 100% of current content]

This is a game marred by a clear disconnect between what narrative the audience expects, and what the creators want to tell. The original horror executed its concept well with its meta elements that weren't present in this new experience turned "deep narrative" about the gentrification of a small community. Remembering its roots, I could count the amount of horror moments in Simulacra 3 with a single-fingered hand. Rook-your character-crumpling like paper could certainly be seen as horror, with his flimsy attempts to push consequences on those around him.

The puzzles felt immature and insulting at best, while tedious and hintless at worst. These ranging from reading two posts on their limited feed to tracing paths that were directly communicated; a confusing case with reviews mentioning the need to "pay close attention." Surprises in narrative were few and far between, boiling down to the Simulacra coming in like a disappointing WWE wrestler that you wished wasn't part of the new arc. Pushed by "Big Horror" in an otherwise new space.

The mixed art form in the single truly interactive camera segment was exciting, teasing more diverse gameplay segments. Pity. That was all. Truly, a pity, with the acting of Ruby and Paul being a joy to see, reminding me of passionate youth theatre. It fell quickly back to its trudging phone interface that felt like a nightmare for subsequent playthroughs. Getting all the ending cards felt like a punishment rather than a reward.

Please purge your mind of previous entries if you're going to give this a go, and be ready to spend more time reading meaningless social feeds to fish for info used in two more obtuse puzzles. Keep in mind, this remains the most expensive entry in the series.

review_text_raw: I love the other Simulacra games, but I waited a while to play this one because it has mixed reviews. I can understand why now and am disappointed...The game feels rushed. It has typos and the dialogue is poor. Gameplay in terms of finding info and doing puzzles is lame/tedious, and there aren't many puzzles at all. Story and characters are underdeveloped. I was also really disappointed to find your choices don't matter that much throughout the game. There are only a few choices that make any difference in dialogue/outcome, which sucks for a game where 90% of the gameplay is choosing dialogue options. I replayed to get all endings and achievements, but we're talking minor changes between outcomes that make replaying the game basically pointless. Overall, not much actually happens to make the game worth your time. Just skip it if you're a fan of the previous games.

review_text_raw:
I was excited for this game's release, but after playing the game I am admittedly disappointed and cannot recommend this game to others. I will mention that the way the game flows it does appear that they either lost funding, ran out of time or there were other extenuating circumstances that caused this severe drop in quality. However, I don't think this is enough to outweigh my experience playing the game.

I will say I do like the idea behind the story and the execution of the beginning of the game. However, the "live" video calls are executed in the worst way possible. No only do they not feel live as the film cuts weren't edited in a way to feel like they are happening in real time but there is also 0 consequences for going inactive and not inputting anything in time. The game will auto-select the best responses every time. It just kills any feeling that these sections were important - for if they were why wasn't there a no-response option specifically for these sections as well? Literally makes these sections all the less intense or important as you can just walk away and still get the proper info/endings. It feels like you worked for nothing if you did try to react in real time to these sections. Not only that but the puzzles that had the least impact on the overall story were the hardest, while puzzles for key evidence/advancement toward an ending are either forced or way too simple to solve. It made the game feel unbalanced and more frustrating than fun. The ending sequence feels more like a footnote rather than a true ending to the game as well.

I hope the developers of the game take note of the criticisms given for this release and I hope that the next SIMULACRA game will not repeat these mistakes. This is a terrible way to end the series so I hope they will make up for this the next time around. I loved the first two games and I'll admit there was promise in this one that just fell flat for multiple reasons.
